learning_objective: 🎯 Go beyond just 'not being sick' and discover how to achieve true holistic wellness through lifestyle choices, hygiene, and mental health care!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Health is not merely the absence of disease. According to WHO, it is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being. Wellness is the active process of making choices toward a healthy life.
These are diseases caused by the way we live—like eating too much junk food, lack of exercise, stress, and poor sleep. Examples include obesity, Type 2 diabetes, and high blood pressure.
Hygiene (daily bathing, washing hands, dental care) prevents individual sickness. Sanitation (safe disposal of waste, clean drinking water) prevents diseases from spreading in the community.
Mental wellness involves managing stress, maintaining a positive attitude, and seeking help when feeling depressed or anxious. It is just as important as physical health.
Taking steps to prevent illnesses before they happen. This includes regular exercise, a balanced diet, vaccination, and maintaining a clean environment.

fun_activity.title: 🧘 The 5-Minute Mind Reset
fun_activity.instructions: Mental wellness is part of health! Sit in a quiet place, close your eyes, and take 10 deep breaths. Focus only on the air going in and out. Notice how much lighter and calmer your mind feels afterward.

exam_tips: 📌 Always quote the WHO definition of health: 'A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being...'
📌 Be ready to list 3 common 'Lifestyle Diseases' and their primary causes (diet and inactivity).
📌 Differentiate between Hygiene (personal habits) and Sanitation (public facilities/waste management).
quick_recap: ⭐ True wellness requires balancing physical fitness, mental peace, and social connections.
⭐ Washing hands with soap is the simplest and most effective way to prevent infections.
⭐ Positive lifestyle choices in youth prevent chronic diseases in old age.
